messages:
Maya K: Pushed the dep bump + follow-up fixes for the review yesterday. Main changes: pinned numpy->2.1.0, split the large request serializer into a helper, and added a unit test for the missing-kv edge-case. CI is running now. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/8423 — can someone eyeball the test shape change and the commit layout? @Alex H @Cheng L
Alex H: Looking now. quick Q: did you intentionally keep the old compat shim? the helper looks fine but that shim could affect latency in Dedicated.
Maya K: Yep — left the shim for backward compat with some Dedicated customers; added an inline comment explaining the reason. Also added a short benchmark and usage note in the PR description. Example to run locally: ```python -m pytest tests/test_helper.py::test_edge --maxfail=1 -q```
Cheng L: Logic looks good to me. Small nit: rename the test to something clearer (e.g. test_helper_edge_missing_kv). Also can you squash the dep-bump commit into the refactor commit? makes bisection easier.
ci-bot: CI/CD: build started for PR #8423 — running 12 jobs.
Alex H: Ran the unit set locally, all green except one flaky integration on arm that I left a comment about. otherwise :+1: pending Cheng's squash.
Samir P: If Cheng gives final LGTM after squash, i'm +1 to merge. Let's gate merging on a short canary at 14:00 PT. who will own canary monitoring?
Maya K: I can own the canary, watch latency/error-rate and post results. plan: merge after Cheng rebases/squashes and approves, then kick the canary. thanks! :rocket:
Cheng L: I'll rebase & squash in ~20m and ping here when done.
ci-bot: CI/CD: all jobs passed for PR #8423 — ready to merge.
Maya K: Merged and started canary: canary/8423. Dashboard -> https://console.redwood/inference/metrics/canary/8423. I'll post an update at ~14:10 with any regressions.
Alex H: Thanks — i'll keep an eye during the sync.
